verdict.wrong_value: NaT is stored as the int64 minimum, so the cast produces a large sentinel instead of a missing value
verdict.rationale: This PR fixes a mishandling of special values (NaT - Not a Time) in timedelta64 data. When xr.polyval processes timedelta64 coordinates containing NaT values, the function _ensure_numeric converts to float using a plain astype(float), which incorrectly converts NaT (stored as int64 minimum) to a large sentinel value instead of NaN. The fix ensures NaT values properly propagate as NaN in the numerical computation, which is essential for correct polynomial evaluation with missing time-based values. This is a clear numerical bug involving improper handling of a special value (NaT/NaN) during type conversion in numerical computation.

verdict.wrong_value: equivalent(np.float64(np.nan), np.float64(np.nan)) returned False instead of True
verdict.rationale: This PR fixes a mishandled special value (NaN) bug. The issue is that when two NumPy scalar NaN values are compared with ==, the result is np.bool_(False) rather than Python bool. In the buggy code, this equality comparison happened before the NaN equivalence check, causing the function to incorrectly return False when comparing two NaN values. The fix reorders the logic to perform the NaN check (using np.isnan()) before the equality comparison, ensuring that equivalent(NaN, NaN) correctly returns True for Python floats, NumPy scalars (float64, float32), and mixed combinations. This is a fundamental numerical correctness issue involving the special value NaN.
